name: Faggen
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Oberinntal valley, featuring vast fields, traditional farms, and breathtaking views of the Kaunergrat mountains.
title: Faggen
metaDescription: Faggen at the gateway to the Kaunertal valley: Landeck district's smallest municipality, sunny Kaunergrat slopes, nature park and glacier highway.
text:
Overview

Faggen is situated at an altitude of 900 meters in the Upper Inn Valley in the district of Landeck, positioned directly at the entrance to the pristine Kaunertal valley. Encompassing an area of only 3.63 square kilometers, Faggen is the geographically smallest municipality in the entire Landeck district. Its approximately 380 residents dwell across the hamlets of Unterfaggen, Oberfaggen, Innergufl, and Außergufl, nestled along the sunny southern foothills of the formidable Kaunergrat mountain range. Framed by terraced meadows and traditional heritage farms, this peaceful mountain farming village preserves genuine rural traditions while serving as an ideal starting point for exploring the Kaunergrat Nature Park and the Kaunertal Glacier.

History

Human settlement on the alluvial cone of the Faggenbach stream reaches back into antiquity, with bronze artifacts proving habitation around 1500 BC. The settlement was first documented in 1433 under the name Trifakken. The name is of Rhaeto-Romanic origin, describing a place at the confluence of branching watercourses, symbolized in the municipal coat of arms by three radiating white streams. For centuries, everyday life was centered on mountain agriculture, cattle breeding, and ingenious traditional irrigation systems known as Waale. Ecclesiastically, Faggen was historically affiliated with Kauns and was transferred to the parish of Prutz in 1947, while the spiritual center of the valley developed around the Church of the Holy Trinity in nearby Feichten. In the hamlet of Unterfaggen, the modern Mariahilf Chapel was constructed between 1975 and 1977, enshrining an eighteenth-century altarpiece alongside a bronze crucifix by Tyrolean sculptor Kassian Erhart.

Getting There

By automobile, travelers take the Inntal motorway A12 or the S16 expressway to the Landeck-Süd/Reschenpass exit, continuing through the Landeck Tunnel along federal road B180 to Prutz. In Prutz, turn onto the L18 Kaunertal road; Faggen lies just a few hundred meters ahead. Rail passengers arrive at the major transport hub Landeck-Zams railway station, served by international Railjet and Eurocity trains. From the station forecourt, VVT regional bus line 210 towards Kaunertal operates regularly, reaching Faggen in approximately twenty minutes. With the local guest card of the Kaunertal and Tiroler Oberland region, public regional bus travel is complimentary for overnight visitors.

Tips

Faggen serves as the gateway to the renowned Kaunertal Glacier Road, one of Europe's most spectacular high-alpine routes, ascending 29 hairpin bends to 2,750 meters at the edge of the Weißseeferner glacier. Highlights include a walk-in glacial crevasse and the barrier-free viewing platform at the Karlesjochbahn cable car at 3,108 meters with panoramas of Austria, Italy, and Switzerland. The nearby Kaunergrat Nature Park Centre at Piller Sattel offers the award-winning 3,000 m Vertical exhibition and the Adlerblick observation terrace. Gentle hiking trails follow historic irrigation channels, lead to the historic pilgrimage sanctuary of Kaltenbrunn, or approach the medieval Berneck Castle in neighboring Kauns. The Kaunertal valley is internationally celebrated as a leading destination for sustainable, accessible alpine travel.
